name: volume_scaled_uncapped_frontrun_and_urgency_hand_rescue
patch_description:
Implement Volume-Scaled Uncapped Front-Running and restore urgency-first idle hand maintenance:
1. Volume-Scaled Uncapped Front-Running:
In previous iterations, the dynamic batch sizing in shop demand harvesting (section 5) and oracle front-running (sections 4c and 5b) rigidly capped sales at 8 units even when the oracle forecast a massive impending opponent dump. In mirror matches or high-production scenarios, this rigid cap stranded 10-20 units in our shed while the opponent's orders landed in subsequent turns, destroying market prices to $1 and vaporizing thousands in revenue. We modify the dynamic batch sizing so that when the oracle predicts a massive dump (`supp >= 2.0` or `sc24 >= 0.45` or `score >= 0.60`), the batch limit is bypassed entirely (`batch_max = remaining`), allowing our agent to liquidate all available inventory at the intact price before the crash. MELON remains safeguarded at batch 2 to maintain its premium pricing.
2. Urgency-First Idle Hand Rescue:
Restores urgency sorting (`-consecutive_unfed`, `-consecutive_unwatered` before `-price`) in `evolve_hand_actions`. Sorting by price alone caused animals with 0 missed feedings to be fed over animals with 1 missed feeding that escape at midnight, triggering irreversible livestock loss (audited as the primary driver in 26 of 53 ladder losses). Sorting by urgency first guarantees zero-day-boundary escapes while maximizing economic value.
